A1.justification: Both 19-page PDFs describe the same SEAG work. The main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–I are available and can be reliably matched despite layout changes and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSM8K and ARC experiments, component ablations, and additional benchmark and prompt-sampling results in Appendices G and H.

after.justification: v2 reports original reasoning experiments and ablations on GSM8K and ARC, appendix analyses, and an additional end-to-end latency experiment in Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 and Algorithm 1 revise expansion-action selection: v1 uniformly samples representatives from semantic clusters, whereas v2 selects a cluster using semantic PUCT and expands using its highest-probability action. The overall gating, clustering and early-stopping framework remains intact.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K mathematical reasoning and ARC science questions, including the same appendix scenarios. The new latency experiment samples existing ARC coverage rather than introducing a distinct task or population.

E2.justification: CoT, CoT-SC, ToT and RAP remain the benchmark comparators, and the new latency comparison uses this same set. The UCT/PUCT and equal-weighting ablations also retain their comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds average end-to-end latency evaluation on 100 randomly selected ARC instances using Llama3-8B-Instruct on one RTX A5000 GPU. This supplements the retained 400-instance benchmark evaluations; existing model configurations and Table A1 hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new latency analysis examines semantic-clustering overhead and decomposes runtime by termination after CoT-SC versus proceeding through SE. Existing entropy analyses, cluster-count studies, token-cost sweeps, component ablations and Appendix H prompt-sampling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E states that results are based on a single run in both versions. v2 adds no repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; its average latency measurements do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, ablation and appendix result values are unchanged. New Table 3 reports latency of 1.43, 13.67, 120.63, 151.19, 76.44 and 38.89 seconds for CoT, CoT-SC, ToT, RAP, SE and SEAG, respectively. New text also reports 2.54 seconds of clustering overhead and approximately 67% termination after CoT-SC.

T1.justification: Appendix C corrects the simulation action expression from max r(s,a) to argmax r(s,a), making it return an action rather than a reward value. This is a local mathematical correction; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about semantic exploration, adaptive gating and early stopping, including the headline 4.3% accuracy improvement and 31% computational cost. The latency results provide additional support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations involving unnecessary search, semantic redundancy and weighted aggregation are retained, as are limitations concerning internal knowledge and discrete final answers. The added latency discussion quantitatively supports the existing efficiency rationale.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract, specifies argmax over DeBERTa outputs for entailment decisions, and documents A5000 hardware for the latency study and in Appendix E. Existing prompts, default hyperparameters and the 832 GPU-hour estimate are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive related-work positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to RAP, ToT, entailment-based semantic clustering and Jang et al.'s predefined-action setting.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized typo and wording corrections, rewrites parts of Section 4.2 and Algorithm 1, clarifies appendix terminology, and adds latency discussion and acknowledgements. The overall section order and Appendix A–I organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adjusts Figure 1, adds latency Table 3, renumbers the former Tables 3–4 as Tables 4–5, relocates existing displays and moves table captions below their tables, including in the appendices. Existing result plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The new latency experiment strengthens the efficiency evidence beyond v1's inference-count and token-cost proxies by including measured clustering overhead. Code-access information and clearer algorithm specification also help reproducibility. The gains are limited: timing covers one configuration, benchmark results remain unchanged and single-run, and the revised expansion-action rule is not separately evaluated.
